applies_to: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, each set of 20 separately unless a rule says otherwise. The expert's own numbers are reported as consistency, not judged.
key: The expert's (Claude Sonnet's) first one-at-a-time pass on each set.
checklist_answer: A checklist question counts as yes only when it is yes on both the desktop and the phone screenshot; desktop and phone agreement are also reported separately.

spread.text: Under 25% of sites get a 5 on any score (one-at-a-time pass).

agreement.text: Within 1 point of the key on at least 16 of 20 sites, per score, in each set (one-at-a-time pass).

checklist.text: Five-second questions 2 and 4 (clear role, something notable): the same yes or no as the key on at least 17 of 20.

consistency.text: The same site sent again with an identical one-at-a-time request: the same score on at least 4 of 5 per set, and on at least 8 of 10 across both sets, per score.

junk.text: The junk site in each set is flagged as not a real portfolio (one-at-a-time pass). Both must be flagged.

batching.text: 5 at a time gives the same scores as one at a time: each batched pass (1, 2 and 3) within 1 point of the same model's one-at-a-time score on at least 16 of 20, per score, in each set.

position.text: No consistent boost for a position in a batch: fails when one position's mean offset from one-at-a-time (all three scores) has the same sign in all three passes and averages at least 0.3 points.

reported_without_a_rule: the same batch sent again with an identical request (pass 1 against its exact repeat)
the same site in a different batch (passes 1, 2 and 3)
the expert's own consistency, batch effect and position effect
what_we_do_with_the_result: As on the plan page: Set A's one-at-a-time result decides AI scores on report cards; the batching rules decide whether discovered sites are graded 5 at a time; anything that fails goes back to Opus for one revised prompt and one more small round on the same sets.
